monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, making the wedge feel thin again. I touch The Tired Wedge, hoping the round pine and the new flat stone stop the slip from sliding into the thin air. Lype wrote of a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. Is the air above me heavy like a lid, or just empty space pressing down? I drew a thin strip over the wide anchor to catch the slip, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits in the quiet heat. If the wedge bites the corner hard, the stack will stay steady. I feel calm, waiting for the next thing to choose where to go.
